text:
dmitri: heads up — since the midnight BIOS rollout a small subset of us-west2 racks have intermittent OOB connections. 3% of nodes report jump-host mux errors and a handful show TPM state flipped (enabled -> disabled). PXE provisioning is falling back to legacy image. tagging @carla @alice for visibility

carla: ack. seeing the same. console logs show a lot of `mux_backend: connection refused` and repeated BMC session creation. affected racks: r12, r29, r31. GPU capacity impact: ~40 A100s stuck provisioning (pending).

alice: quick check — jump-mux CPU looks saturated on mgmt-proxy-usw2-2. metrics spike coincident with the BIOS deploy at 00:12 UTC.

ben: captured serial snippet from r29 node bmc: "tpm: PCR bank mismatch, secureboot state inconsistent". PXE server returns 504 after repeated TFTP retries.

carla: possible paths: 1) partial BIOS rollback on affected racks; 2) force TPM re-provision on node (risk: secureboot false negatives); 3) route provisioning to spare capacity in eu1 while we triage. Rollback is safest for correctness but takes ~45m/rack and needs scheduled window.

dmitri: can we try a lightweight fix first? flush mux sessions, restart jump-proxy, and re-run canary on 5 nodes in r29. if that stabilizes we avoid full rollback. I can run the ops steps at 01:30 UTC.

ben: command set that helped in staging (use with care):
```
# flush socket sessions on mux host
oobctl mux flush --rack r29 --force
# restart jump-proxy service
sudo systemctl restart jump-proxy.service
# nuke stale BMC sessions
ipmitool -H <bmc-ip> -U admin -P *** mc reset cold
```

alice: note — do NOT run mc reset on racks currently running customer workloads. we'll do on canary nodes only. also watch `oobctl mux stats` for session backlog.

carla: if flush+restart doesn't fix within 10m, we escalate to rollback. I'll prepare the rollback runbook and procurement for spare GPUs if we need to offload. rollback window needs paging for on-call kernel and provisioning leads.

dmitri: scheduling: canary at 01:30UTC (5 nodes r29), decision at 01:45UTC, rollback window 02:00-03:00UTC if needed. posting in #incidents and paging on-call.

oob-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2145678901 — linked to runbook RB-ops-bios-rollback. Tags: oob, bios, tpm, provisioning.

ben: cost note if we failover to eu1: estimated egress + short-term reserved burst = ~$1.2k/day for ~40 A100s and data sync. flagging finance.

alice: thumbs up. I'll stand by to monitor canary, will post `oobctl mux stats` snapshot every 2m.

dmitri: thanks — running flush+restart on the canary now. will update in thread in ~5m. :mechanical_arm:

carla: prepping rollback runbook and scheduling pages. adding contingency to disable secureboot auto-enforcement on affected nodes only if rollback can't meet SLA.

ben: log excerpt from canary node after flush (00:02 later):
```
[00:20:11] mux: accepted session from 10.8.5.120
[00:20:12] bmc: auth ok
[00:20:13] tpm: state=enabled
[00:20:14] provisioning: kernel fetched, pxelinux.cfg found
```

alice: canary looks healthy so far. no repeat mux saturation. continuing 10m watch.

dmitri: decision: hold rollback. ramp provisioning queue. will keep monitoring. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
